headline: Safety Score counts each open question once, and /coverage/ publishes the three numbers behind each grade.
fieldNotes: Most of the week's Safety Score work went into one question: what is missing, and who is responsible? The publication now counts each open question once at the asset that roots it, splits the total into open questions, not disclosed by issuers and documentation gaps, and refuses to print a zero when a publication predates the counts. Documentation gaps now carry policy reasons, a fail-closed card label and a durable lapse. No score moved.

summary.label: Open-question counts
summary.description: /coverage/ now opens with three server-counted numbers: open questions, not disclosed by issuers, and documentation gaps. Each is counted once at its root asset, and an older publication reads as unavailable, never zero.

summary.label: Report-cards API 9
summary.description: The report-cards API gains an additive openEvidence block with the same three totals, owner and reason rows, the issuer review window and per-card rows. Scores, grades and evidence levels stay untouched.

summary.label: Documentation gaps
summary.description: A policy-owned documentation class now marks the open questions whose resolution cannot materially move a score, under six published reasons and two strict bars. Pricing, causes, caps and evidence levels stay byte-identical, and a card reads "limited · documentation gaps only" only when every limiting witness is documentation.

summary.label: Missing-data registry v3
summary.description: The curation registry gains documentation and issuer bands, keys its questions through the shared counting authority, and drops a supplement only when every obligation it carries is already a compiled task, so the worklist shows 72 supplements instead of 469 on the current capture.

summary.label: Scores dataset v2
summary.description: The scores dataset display projection carries the same totals with their semantics, plus a machine-readable reason when a generation predates them, so missing counts never read as zero.

summary.label: Plainer gap language
summary.description: A cause-A pillar gap now reads "data pipeline unavailable" rather than implying an issuer omission, and one shared vocabulary names all three buckets on the page and in its explanations.
